# Ableton MCP Extended — Quick Reference

Compact cheatsheet for Ableton MCP Extended tools.
Generated from MCP tool decorators and command registry.

## Top Commands by Category

*(UDP = low-latency fire-and-forget, TCP = reliable request/response)*

### Session Setup

- `create_audio_track` [TCP] — Create a new audio track in the Ableton session.
- `create_clip` [TCP] — Create a new MIDI clip in the specified track and clip slot.
- `create_midi_track` [TCP] — Create a new MIDI track in the Ableton session.
- `create_scene` [TCP] — Create a new scene.
- `delete_all_tracks` [TCP] — Delete all tracks in the Ableton session.
- `delete_track` [TCP] — Delete a track from the session.
- `duplicate_track` [TCP] — Duplicate a track.
- `set_tempo` [TCP] — Set the tempo of the Ableton session.
- `set_track_color` [TCP] — Set the color of a track.
- `set_track_fold` [TCP] — Set the fold state of a track.
- `set_track_monitoring_state` [TCP] — Set track monitoring state (audio tracks only).
- `set_track_name` [TCP] — Set the name of a track.

### Arrangement

- `create_locator` [TCP] — Create a locator at a specific bar.
- `get_playhead_position` [TCP] — Get the current playhead position in the Ableton session.
- `jump_to_locator` [TCP] — Jump to a locator.
- `set_loop` [TCP] — Set arrangement loop region.
- `set_playhead_position` [TCP] — Set the playhead position to a specific bar and beat.
- `start_playback` [TCP] — Start playing the Ableton session.
- `start_recording` [TCP] — Start recording. Playback will also start if not already playing.
- `stop_playback` [TCP] — Stop playing the Ableton session.
- `stop_recording` [TCP] — Stop recording. Playback continues.

### Mixing

- `apply_crossfader_sweep` [TCP] — Sweep the crossfader from one position to another over time.
- `apply_send_sweep` [TCP] — Sweep a send amount from one value to another over time.
- `get_level_snapshot` [TCP] — Get current meter levels for master and all tracks.
- `get_track_sends` [TCP] — Get all send amounts for a track with return track names.
- `set_crossfader_position` [TCP] — Set the master crossfader position (0.0-1.0).
- `set_master_volume` [UDP] — Set master track volume (normalized 0.0-1.0).
- `set_track_mute` [UDP] — Mute or unmute a track.
- `set_track_pan` [UDP] — Set track panning.
- `set_track_solo` [UDP] — Solo or unsolo a track.
- `set_track_volume` [UDP] — Set track volume (normalized 0.0-1.0).

### UDP

- `fire_clip` [UDP] — Start playing a clip.
- `set_clip_launch_mode` [UDP] — Set clip launch mode.
- `set_device_parameter` [UDP] — Set a device parameter value (normalized 0.0-1.0).
- `set_master_volume` [UDP] — Set master track volume (normalized 0.0-1.0).
- `set_send_amount` [UDP] — Set send amount to a return track.
- `set_track_arm` [UDP] — Arm or unarm a track for recording.
- `set_track_mute` [UDP] — Mute or unmute a track.
- `set_track_pan` [UDP] — Set track panning.
- `set_track_solo` [UDP] — Solo or unsolo a track.
- `set_track_volume` [UDP] — Set track volume (normalized 0.0-1.0).

### Effects

- `delete_device` [TCP] — Delete a device from a track.
- `duplicate_device` [TCP] — Duplicate a device to another track.
- `get_device_parameters` [TCP] — Get all parameters for a specific device on a track.
- `load_instrument_or_effect` [TCP] — Load an instrument or effect onto a track using its URI.
- `load_instrument_preset` [TCP] — Load a preset for a device on a track by name.
- `move_device` [TCP] — Move a device to a new position in the device chain.

### MIDI

- `add_notes_to_clip` [TCP] — Add MIDI notes to a clip.
- `create_drum_pattern` [TCP] — Create a common drum pattern from a template.
- `delete_notes_from_clip` [TCP] — Delete specific notes from a clip by indices.
- `get_clip_notes` [TCP] — Get all notes from a clip.
- `quantize_clip` [TCP] — Quantize notes in a clip.
- `set_global_quantization` [TCP] — Set the global quantization for clip launching.
- `transpose_clip` [TCP] — Transpose all notes in a clip.

## Transport Rules

- **UDP**: Fire-and-forget, low latency (~0.2ms), no response
  - Use for: parameter changes, track controls, clip triggering
  - Only 10 commands support UDP (listed above)

- **TCP**: Request/response, reliable (~20-50ms), awaits ACK
  - Use for: all state-querying, creation, deletion, modifications
  - Required for: `get_*`, `delete_*`, `create_*`, `quantize`, `undo/redo`, recording

CAUTION: NEVER use UDP for `get_*`, `delete_*`, `quantize`, `undo/redo`, or recording operations.
